patients.summary: Schoolteacher in Belchertown with schizophrenia stable on risperidone and hereditary angioedema, who over ten years with the practice is diagnosed with PCOS, binge eating disorder, a prolactin-secreting microadenoma and pulmonary arterial hypertension, and has two high-risk pregnancies, the first ending in severe preeclampsia. Last seen after an ED visit for a lip and tongue attack of HAE; allergy referral open.

documents.title: New patient request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 26 y/o teacher, recently moved to Belchertown, looking for a primary care doctor. Explained membership and that insurance still covers labs, specialists and meds. She would like to sign up. Booked new patient visit 9/13 at 8:00 so she can be done before school pickup duty. Release signed over the phone for her old primary care office; request faxed today. She mentioned a psychiatrist she already sees and that she carries an injectable for a swelling condition, will bring the box.

conditions.label: Hereditary angioedema
conditions.note: C1 inhibitor deficiency; mother and brother affected

medications.sig: Inject 30 mg under the skin at onset of an attack; may repeat in 6 hours, no more than 3 doses in 24 hours

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26-year-old woman, elementary school teacher, joining the practice after a move to Belchertown.

PMH
1. Schizophrenia. First episode in her early twenties. Sees an outside psychiatrist every few months who writes her risperidone. She describes herself as well; no voices or paranoia in years, sleeping fine, working full time. Insight good.
2. Hereditary angioedema, C1 inhibitor deficiency. Diagnosed as a teenager, worked up after her mother and brother were diagnosed. Gets a swollen hand or a belly attack a few times a year, never her throat so far. Uses icatibant at home and it works within a couple of hours. Has not seen an immunologist since college and would like us to handle refills.
No surgeries.

Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily; icatibant 30 mg SC prn attack; prenatal vitamin daily (OTC, takes it 'to be safe').
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: father with schizophrenia. Mother and younger brother with HAE.
SH: teaches 2nd grade. Married. Never smoked, no alcohol, no drugs. Walks most evenings.
GYN: periods present, not always regular. No contraception.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well-appearing, calm, appropriate, linear thought. HEENT normal, no lip or tongue swelling today. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities without edema. Skin without rash.

A/P
- Schizophrenia, stable on risperidone per psychiatry. Will get a release so their notes come here. Baseline metabolic labs given the antipsychotic: A1c, lipids, CMP, CBC.
- HAE: will take over icatibant refills. Reviewed attack plan; ED for any throat tightness, voice change or trouble swallowing even if she has injected.
- Prevention: HIV and hep C screening today. Pap history to come with old records. Flu shot next nurse visit once supply arrives.
- BMI 27. Discussed activity and food choices briefly.
RTC 1 year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Michelle, all of your blood work from Tuesday came back in the normal range: blood count, kidney and liver tests, sugar (A1c), thyroid and cholesterol. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Since risperidone can nudge weight, sugar and cholesterol over time, we'll repeat the sugar and cholesterol once a year. Nice to meet you.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
38 pages received by fax from previous primary care office. Highlights abstracted for the PCP:
- Pap smear 04/2015: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Tdap 2014.
- HAE noted on problem list since adolescence; icatibant last filled 06/2016.
- Schizophrenia, managed by psychiatry; risperidone 4 mg.
- No surgeries, no drug allergies.
Originals filed under media.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after school for influenza vaccine. Screening questions negative, no egg or vaccine reactions. Given L deltoid IM, lot logged. VIS given. Waited 15 minutes, fine.

documents.title: Psychiatry update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient psychiatry, visit of 11/29/2016.

Dear colleague, thank you for taking on Ms. Mazur's primary care. I have followed her for schizophrenia for several years. She remains in sustained remission of positive symptoms on risperidone 4 mg at bedtime, with good function at work and at home. No extrapyramidal symptoms; AIMS 0. She knows to call if sleep falls apart or suspiciousness returns, her early signs. I see her every three months. I appreciate the yearly glucose and lipid monitoring on your end.

Outpatient psychiatrist

documents.title: Prior authorization: icatibant
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Specialty pharmacy faxed the annual prior authorization form for icatibant. Completed with diagnosis of hereditary angioedema type I, attack frequency a few per year, home use. PCP signed. Approval returned same afternoon, good for 12 months. Pt aware her refill ships Thursday.

documents.title: Hand swelling
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Woke up with my right hand puffed up like a glove. It's one of my attacks, no hives, nothing in my throat. I gave myself the shot at 6 and it's already starting to go down. I have one syringe left, could you send a refill so I have two again?

documents.title: RE: Hand swelling
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad it's settling. Refill sent to the specialty pharmacy. Same rule as always: anything with your lips, tongue, throat or voice, go to the ED.

documents.title: Psychiatry update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry, visit of 06/06/2017. Ms. Mazur continues well on risperidone 4 mg nightly. End of the school year stress handled without symptoms. Mood euthymic, no psychotic features. No movement side effects. Plan unchanged; return in three months.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here before school for her yearly visit.

Interval: three swelling episodes this year, two hands and one belly, all treated at home with icatibant, none involving the face. Psychiatry following, doing well. Cycles still unpredictable, sometimes 6 to 8 weeks apart; not trying to conceive, not avoiding it either.

Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily, icatibant prn, prenatal vitamin.
PHQ-9 2.

Exam: comfortable. HEENT, neck normal. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema. Skin: a few comedones along the jaw.

Plan
- Metabolic monitoring for risperidone: A1c, lipids, CMP drawn.
- HAE: two syringes on hand, confirmed.
- Cycles: she would rather watch for now. Revisit if they space out further.
- Flu vaccine given. Pap up to date (2015).
See in a year.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Michelle, sugar, cholesterol, kidney and liver tests are all normal again this year. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Prior authorization: icatibant
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Annual icatibant PA renewal faxed by specialty pharmacy. Completed and signed by PCP. Approved 2/1, pharmacy aware.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28 y/o here about darker, coarser hair on her upper lip and chin over the past year that she now has to remove every morning, plus breakouts along the jawline that drugstore washes and creams have not touched. Periods have spread further apart, now sometimes two months between, occasionally a skipped month. Wonders if something hormonal is going on and whether it matters for having kids someday. No headaches, no vision change, no nipple discharge.

Exam: coarse terminal hairs upper lip and chin, mild papular acne along the mandible. Thyroid normal. Abdomen soft.

A/P: hirsutism with acne and oligomenorrhea, PCOS most likely. Her mother sounds like she had similar features. Given the HAE (estrogen products can provoke attacks) and the risperidone, I'd like endocrinology to do the workup and own the treatment choice. Referral placed. She will keep a period calendar.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group. Date of service 07/02/2018. Reason: referred by her primary care physician for unwanted hair and acne.

HPI: Ms. Mazur, 28, reports roughly twelve months of increasingly coarse hair on the upper lip and chin that she removes daily, and a flare of acne along the jaw that over-the-counter topicals have not improved. Menses have become erratic, at times every second month, at times absent. She is worried about long-term consequences and about her fertility. She denies galactorrhea, headache and visual symptoms. Not using contraception.

PMH: schizophrenia on risperidone 4 mg daily; hereditary angioedema with icatibant as needed. No surgeries.
Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily, icatibant 30 mg SC prn, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.
FH: her mother had the same pattern of facial hair and acne in her twenties. Father schizophrenia. Mother and brother HAE.

Exam: BMI 27. Mild facial acne. Excess terminal hair on the upper lip and a periumbilical escutcheon. Pelvic examination normal. Remainder unremarkable.

Office testing: fasting glucose normal. Urine hCG negative.

Impression: clinical hyperandrogenism with oligomenorrhea; polycystic ovary syndrome is suspected. Need to exclude nonclassic CAH, thyroid disease and hyperprolactinemia, and document the androgen level.

Plan: total testosterone, DHEA-S, 17-hydroxyprogesterone (early morning), TSH and prolactin next week. Will review results by phone visit.

Cc: primary care

documents.title: Outside lab results
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body: Results from outside endocrinology, copied to primary care. Total testosterone 71 ng/dL (H). DHEA-S 212 mcg/dL. 17-OH progesterone 88 ng/dL. TSH within range. Prolactin 31 ng/mL (H). Endocrinology will contact the patient.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group. Telephone follow-up 08/13/2018.

Results reviewed with Ms. Mazur. Total testosterone mildly elevated at 71. DHEA-S and early-morning 17-OHP normal, so no adrenal source or nonclassic CAH. TSH normal. Prolactin 31, a modest rise in keeping with risperidone; no symptoms of a pituitary process, no imaging needed now.

Assessment: polycystic ovary syndrome by Rotterdam criteria (oligo-ovulation with clinical and biochemical hyperandrogenism, mimics excluded).

Discussion: the usual first-line combined hormonal pill is not a good fit because estrogen can worsen hereditary angioedema. She does not want a medication right now. We talked about laser or electrolysis for the facial hair, steady activity and food habits, and the yearly glucose screening her PCP already does. On fertility: ovulation is irregular, so conception may take longer, but many women with PCOS conceive; she should let us know when she is ready to try.

Follow up as needed. Cc: primary care.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit.

Since last year: saw endocrinology this summer, now carries a diagnosis of PCOS. Their letter is in the chart: no pill because of the HAE; she is looking into laser treatment for her lip and chin. Cycles still every 5 to 9 weeks. Two hand attacks this year, home icatibant. Psychiatry steady.

Meds unchanged: risperidone 4 mg, icatibant prn, prenatal vitamin.
PHQ-9 3.

Exam: well. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft. No edema. Mild jawline acne.

A/P
- PCOS: A1c and lipids today, matters more now with both PCOS and an antipsychotic.
- Schizophrenia: stable, psych following.
- HAE: refills current.
- Flu shot today. Pap due next year at 30, will do cotesting then.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c, cholesterol, kidney and liver tests normal. Keep up the evening walks.

documents.title: Psychiatry update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry, visit of 11/27/2018. Doing well; new PCOS diagnosis noted from endocrinology, and we discussed that risperidone can raise prolactin, which may contribute to cycle changes. She prefers to stay on risperidone given years of stability, and I agree. No psychotic symptoms. Continue 4 mg nightly. Next visit February.

documents.title: Belly attack
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Had one of my stomach attacks this afternoon, the cramping kind, came on during recess duty. Used icatibant at 3:30 and by dinner it was mostly gone. No swelling anywhere else. That leaves me with one pen. Can you send another to the specialty pharmacy?

documents.title: RE: Belly attack
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sorry you had a rough afternoon. Refill request sent to the PCP and approved, the pharmacy will call you to set up delivery. If belly pain does not ease after a dose, or you get a second wave, please call us or go to the ED.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in wanting to talk about food. Since around the holidays she has had evenings where she eats far past full, fast, alone, and feels she cannot stop; afterward she feels awful about it. Roughly once a week, sometimes more. No vomiting, no laxatives, no punishing workouts afterward. Not restricting during the day beyond skipping lunch on busy days. Mood otherwise okay, PHQ-9 4. No voices or suspiciousness, sleeping normally, adherent to risperidone.

Exam: weight steady compared with fall. Otherwise not examined in detail.

A/P: recurrent episodes that sound like binge eating. Her psychiatrist knows her best and can sort out diagnosis and whether therapy or medication fits alongside the risperidone. With her permission I sent a message to psychiatry today; she has a visit with them in July and will raise it herself as well. Not starting anything here.

documents.title: Psychiatry follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient psychiatry. Date of service 07/01/2019.

Ms. Mazur, 29, followed here for schizophrenia, was diagnosed with PCOS by endocrinology last summer. For about six months she has had episodes at least weekly of eating a clearly larger amount than most people would in the same situation, with a sense of being unable to stop, followed by intense distress and guilt. She does not purge, use laxatives or exercise to compensate.

Psychotic symptoms remain in remission on risperidone 4 mg nightly. Mood mildly low around the episodes only.
BMI 27. Exam unremarkable.
Labs from 06/24: CBC, TSH, fasting glucose and lipid profile all within normal limits.
FH: father schizophrenia; mother and brother hereditary angioedema; mother PCOS.
Never smoker, no alcohol. Teacher.

Assessment: binge eating disorder; schizophrenia in sustained remission.

Plan: referral to a therapist in our group for CBT focused on binge eating, weekly to start. I am not recommending lisdexamfetamine given her psychotic illness. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Return in 3 months. Cc: primary care.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Just turned 30. Yearly exam with first co-test.

Interval: psychiatry diagnosed binge eating disorder in July and she has been in weekly CBT since August; episodes down to every couple of weeks. Psychotic symptoms quiet. One belly attack in March treated at home. PCOS unchanged, cycles 5 to 8 weeks.

Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily, icatibant prn, prenatal vitamin.
PHQ-9 3.

Exam: well. Thyroid normal. Breasts without masses. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap with HPV collected. No edema.

A/P
- Cervical screening: co-test sent.
- BED, schizophrenia: per psychiatry, doing well.
- PCOS + antipsychotic: A1c, lipids, CMP today.
- Flu vaccine given.

documents.title: Pap and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap was normal and HPV was not found, so the next one is due in five years. A1c, cholesterol and chemistries are normal too.

documents.title: Psychiatry update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry, visit 12/03/2019. Psychosis in remission on risperidone 4 mg nightly. Binge eating: in weekly CBT with our therapist since August; episodes have dropped from weekly to about twice a month. Mood stable. Continue plan; return in 3 months.

documents.title: Prior authorization: icatibant
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Yearly PA renewal for icatibant from the specialty pharmacy. Insurer now wants attack count for the past 12 months: 3 per chart and portal messages. Submitted, approved 2/12. Pharmacy notified.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit; she is at home, teaching remotely this spring.

Over about six months her cycles have become more irregular than her usual PCOS pattern, and she has noticed milky fluid from both nipples, sometimes on her bra without squeezing. In the past couple of months, new frontal headaches a few times a week. Vision normal, no double vision. No new medications; risperidone unchanged. She has not done a pregnancy test lately.

Observed: alert, well, speech normal. Full extraocular movements on screen, no facial asymmetry.

A/P: galactorrhea with oligomenorrhea and headaches. On risperidone, which raises prolactin, but the new headaches make me want a pituitary evaluation. She already knows the endocrinologist from 2018; referral back sent today, asked for a prompt slot. Pregnancy test to be done with their labs. Go to the ED for vision loss or a sudden severe headache.

orders.order: MRI pituitary with and without contrast

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group. Date of service 06/26/2020.

Known to me with PCOS since 2018. Sent back by her PCP: for six months, cycles more irregular, galactorrhea, and recently headaches. No visual disturbance. Remains on risperidone 4 mg daily.

BP 120/78, HR 72, BMI 26.
Neuro: cranial nerves intact, visual fields full to confrontation, no focal deficit.

Labs today: prolactin 220 ng/mL. TSH 2.5 mIU/L. FSH 4.2 and LH 3.8 mIU/mL. Serum beta-hCG under 5.

Assessment: prolactin of 220 is higher than risperidone alone usually produces, and with headaches a lactotroph adenoma needs to be excluded.
Plan: dedicated pituitary MRI with and without contrast. Will call with results and treatment plan. Cc: primary care; psychiatry.

reports.study: MRI pituitary with and without contrast
reports.text: Indication: hyperprolactinemia, headaches. Technique: thin-section sagittal and coronal T1 and T2 imaging of the sella before and after gadolinium, with dynamic coronal post-contrast sequence; limited axial images of the brain. Findings: 3 mm hypoenhancing focus in the left aspect of the anterior pituitary on dynamic images, consistent with a microadenoma. Gland height normal. Infundibulum midline. Optic chiasm normal in position and signal, no contact. Cavernous sinuses normal. Visualized brain parenchyma normal.
reports.conclusion: 3 mm pituitary microadenoma. No mass effect.

documents.title: Pituitary MRI
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Outside imaging center report received, copied to PCP. 3 mm pituitary microadenoma; chiasm clear.

medications.sig: Take 1/2 tablet (0.25 mg) by mouth twice weekly

documents.title: Endocrinology telephone follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group. Telephone visit 07/17/2020.

Reviewed MRI: 3 mm microadenoma, no chiasmal contact. With prolactin 220 and symptoms, diagnosis is a prolactin-secreting microadenoma, likely amplified by risperidone.

I spoke with her psychiatrist before this call. Given years of stability, we agreed not to change the antipsychotic. Start cabergoline at a low dose, 0.25 mg twice weekly, and watch closely for any return of psychotic symptoms, which dopamine agonists can provoke. She and her husband know the warning signs and will call psychiatry first.

Recheck prolactin in 3 months. No visual field testing needed for a lesion this size. Cc: PCP, psychiatry.

documents.title: Medication list update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Endocrinology letter received: 3 mm prolactin-secreting microadenoma, cabergoline 0.25 mg twice weekly started 7/17. Called pt to reconcile. She picked it up Saturday, took the first half-tablet with dinner, mild nausea only. Psychiatry aware. Med list updated.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group. Visit 10/16/2020.

Three months on cabergoline 0.25 mg twice weekly. Nipple discharge has stopped. Headaches gone since August. Cycles now every 5 to 6 weeks. Psychiatry reports no change in mental status; she feels herself. No nausea or dizziness on the drug.

Prolactin 38 ng/mL, down from 220.

Plan: continue current dose. Prolactin again in 5 months. Cc: PCP.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Masked visit, screening negative at the door.

Interval: endocrinology found a 3 mm prolactin-secreting microadenoma in July; on cabergoline 0.25 mg twice weekly, prolactin now 38, discharge and headaches resolved. Psychiatry aware and she has been stable. CBT for binge eating ongoing by video, episodes uncommon now. Back in the classroom with hybrid teaching.

Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily, cabergoline 0.25 mg twice weekly (endo), icatibant prn, prenatal vitamin.
PHQ-9 2.

Exam: well. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema.

A/P
- Prolactinoma: per endocrinology.
- Metabolic monitoring: labs today.
- Flu vaccine given. COVID vaccine once available to teachers.
- Medication list updated with cabergoline.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Michelle, your labs from Tuesday are all normal, including sugar and cholesterol.

documents.title: Psychiatry update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry, telehealth visit 01/05/2021. Six months on low-dose cabergoline with no change in mental state; no hallucinations, no paranoid thinking, sleep regular. Binge eating episodes now less than monthly after CBT; she is tapering therapy to every other week. Continue risperidone 4 mg nightly. Return in 3 months.

documents.title: Prior authorization: icatibant
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Icatibant PA renewal submitted; one attack in the past year documented. Approved 2/10.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body: Outside endocrinology group. Visit 03/12/2021. Doing well on cabergoline 0.25 mg twice weekly. No galactorrhea or headache. Cycles roughly monthly. Prolactin 19 ng/mL, normal. Continue; recheck in 6 months. Cc: PCP.

documents.title: COVID vaccine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got both Pfizer shots at the pharmacy through the teacher program, 3/4 and 3/25. Just a sore arm and a tired day after the second. Uploading a photo of my card.

documents.title: RE: COVID vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks, both doses entered in your record.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Since around December she gets winded going up the stairs at school, and it has crept up so that the second flight now stops her. Assumed she was out of shape from the remote year, but walking more has not helped. No chest pain, no palpitations, sleeps flat, ankles not swollen. No cough, no wheeze, no fever. Never smoked. No throat or face swelling. COVID vaccinated in March, no known infection.

Exam: comfortable at rest, speaking full sentences. Heart regular, no murmur heard. Lungs clear throughout. No calf tenderness, no edema. Walked the hallway with me, no desaturation by finger probe.

A/P: progressive exertional dyspnea in a young never-smoker with a normal resting exam. Anemia is the quick thing to exclude: CBC today. Otherwise this needs a proper cardiopulmonary evaluation; referral to pulmonology placed, they can arrange imaging and echo together. ED for chest pain, fainting or breathlessness at rest.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count is normal, so this is not anemia. Pulmonology has your referral; their office should call you within the week.

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Prominent central pulmonary arteries with dilation of the main pulmonary artery segment. Heart size within normal limits. Lungs clear, no effusion or pneumothorax. Bones unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Prominent pulmonary vasculature and enlarged main pulmonary artery, suggesting pulmonary hypertension.

reports.text: Left ventricle normal in size, wall thickness and systolic function; no regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricular hypertrophy. Valves structurally normal. No pericardial effusion. Atrial septum intact by color Doppler.
reports.conclusion: Right ventricular hypertrophy with structurally and functionally normal left ventricle.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm. Right axis deviation. Normal intervals.

documents.title: Pulmonology consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group. Seen 06/21/2021 at the request of her primary care physician.

HPI: 31-year-old teacher with six months of worsening breathlessness. It began with stairs and now occurs walking on level ground at a normal pace. No chest pain, palpitations, orthopnea or leg swelling.
PMH: schizophrenia, hereditary angioedema, PCOS, binge eating disorder, prolactin-secreting microadenoma.
Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily, cabergoline 0.25 mg twice weekly, icatibant prn, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.
FH: a sister died suddenly in her early thirties of what the family was told was an undiagnosed heart problem.
SH: never smoker; no drug use; no occupational or environmental exposures.

Exam: mildly tachypneic at rest. JVP elevated. S1 normal, loud palpable P2, no murmur or rub. Lungs clear. No edema, no cyanosis or clubbing.

Studies today: chest film shows prominent pulmonary vasculature and a dilated main PA. Echo shows RV hypertrophy and a normal LV. ECG with right axis deviation.

Impression: pulmonary hypertension, precapillary pattern suspected given the normal left heart. Her sister's death raises concern for a heritable form.

Plan: urgent referral to the regional pulmonary hypertension center for right heart catheterization and full workup. Advised no heavy exertion until seen. Cc: PCP.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth daily
medications.reason: pulmonary arterial hypertension; prescribed by PH center
stopped by PH center as an ergot-derived agent

reports.text: Right internal jugular venous access under ultrasound guidance. Resting hemodynamics: RA mean 7 mmHg, PA mean 41 mmHg, PA wedge 9 mmHg, cardiac output 4.6 L/min by thermodilution, PVR 7.0 Wood units. Inhaled nitric oxide vasoreactivity test negative. No complications.
Ventilation and perfusion images in standard projections. Perfusion is homogeneous with no segmental or subsegmental defects. Ventilation normal.
reports.conclusion: No mismatched perfusion defects; chronic thromboembolic disease not suggested.

reports.text: FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC within normal limits. No bronchodilator response.

documents.title: Pulmonary hypertension center evaluation
documents.author: pulmonary hypertension
documents.body:
Regional pulmonary hypertension center. Evaluation 07/13/2021.

Referred by outside pulmonology with dyspnea, RV hypertrophy and a dilated PA. WHO functional class III.

Right heart cath: RA 7, mPAP 41, PAWP 9, CO 4.6, PVR 7.0 WU; negative vasoreactivity. V/Q scan without mismatched defects. Spirometry normal. NT-proBNP 410 pg/mL. Six-minute walk 410 m without desaturation.

Diagnosis: pulmonary arterial hypertension, intermediate risk. Her sister's sudden death is noted.

Treatment: initial dual oral therapy would be usual, but endothelin receptor antagonists are teratogenic and she tells us she hopes to have children. Starting tadalafil 40 mg daily alone, with close follow-up. Cabergoline stopped as a precaution because ergot-derived dopamine agonists have been linked to pulmonary and valvular disease; at her dose a causal role is unlikely, and her endocrinologist agrees.

Pregnancy: we explained plainly that pregnancy with PAH carries a serious risk to her life and recommended reliable contraception; estrogen-free options were reviewed because of her HAE. She understands and does not want contraception at this time. If she becomes pregnant she should contact us immediately.

Return in 3 months. Cc: PCP, outside pulmonology, endocrinology.

documents.title: Medication list update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: PH center letter received. Tadalafil 40 mg daily started 7/13 through their specialty pharmacy; first shipment delivered per pt. Cabergoline stopped. Med list reconciled. Pt reminded: no nitroglycerin-type medicines with tadalafil, and to tell any ED that she takes it.

documents.title: PH center follow-up
documents.author: pulmonary hypertension
documents.body: Regional pulmonary hypertension center. Visit 10/19/2021. Three months on tadalafil 40 mg daily. Climbing one flight now without stopping; teaching full days. Mild headache the first two weeks, gone. Functional class II. Six-minute walk 455 m (from 410). NT-proBNP 240 (from 410). Continue tadalafil. We again discussed pregnancy risk and contraception; her position is unchanged. Next visit in about a year, sooner if symptoms change. Cc: PCP.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body: Outside endocrinology group. Visit 10/26/2021. Cabergoline was stopped in July by the PH center. Off treatment, prolactin is 48 ng/mL, a modest rise partly from risperidone. No galactorrhea, no headaches, cycles about every 5 weeks. With a 3 mm lesion and no symptoms, observation is reasonable. Recheck in 6 to 12 months, sooner with symptoms or pregnancy. Cc: PCP.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Big year. Pulmonology found pulmonary hypertension in June; PH center cath in July confirmed pulmonary arterial hypertension and she has been on tadalafil 40 mg since. Breathing much better, one flight without stopping, class II per their October note. Cabergoline was stopped; endocrinology is watching the prolactin (48 in October) without treatment. Psychiatry stable, binge episodes rare.

We talked about pregnancy. She has heard the PH team's warning clearly and still hopes for a child; she is not using contraception. I told her I respect the decision, that she should call the PH team and us the day of any positive test, and that I'd help set up a high-risk OB right away.

Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily, tadalafil 40 mg daily, icatibant prn, prenatal vitamin.
PHQ-9 3.

Exam: comfortable, no tachypnea at rest. Heart regular, loud P2. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
- PAH: per PH center.
- Metabolic labs today.
- Flu and COVID booster given today.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All normal: cholesterol, A1c, kidney and liver tests.

documents.title: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Two positive home tests this morning. Last period started December 14. I know what the PH team said. I'm calling them when they open at 8 but wanted you to know first. What do I do with my medicines?

conditions.label: Supervision of high risk pregnancy, unspecified, unspecified trimester

documents.title: Call re: pregnancy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called her back. About 3 weeks from LMP 12/14/21. She feels well, breathing unchanged. She already left a message with the PH center.

Medications: keep taking tadalafil and risperidone until the PH team and her psychiatrist say otherwise, do not stop either on her own. Continue prenatal vitamin. Icatibant: keep it for attacks and let OB know if she needs it.

Placed urgent referral to maternal-fetal medicine at the hospital that works with the PH center; called their intake line myself to flag PAH. She will message psychiatry and endocrinology today. She asked whether we would still be her doctor through this: yes, we'll stay in the loop for everything outside the pregnancy.

reports.text: Single intrauterine gestation. Cardiac activity present. Crown-rump length consistent with 8 weeks 0 days, concordant with LMP. Adnexa unremarkable. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Viable single intrauterine pregnancy, about 8 weeks.

documents.title: Maternal-fetal medicine consultation
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body:
Maternal-fetal medicine, regional hospital. Visit 02/08/2022.

G1, about 8 weeks by LMP 12/14/2021, confirmed by ultrasound today. Pulmonary arterial hypertension, functional class II on tadalafil 40 mg daily; schizophrenia stable on risperidone 4 mg; hereditary angioedema with icatibant as needed; PCOS; 3 mm prolactin-secreting microadenoma off treatment.

Counseled together with the PH center by phone about the substantial maternal risk in PAH, including the option of ending the pregnancy. She wishes to continue.

Plan: co-management with the PH center, visits every 2 to 4 weeks; continue tadalafil, risperidone and prenatal vitamin; serial echocardiography; delivery planning at our hospital with cardiac anesthesia; HAE plan to be written with the delivery team. Endocrinology: no routine prolactin checks in pregnancy; report headache or visual change. Cc: PCP, PH center, psychiatry.

documents.title: Prenatal visit note
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body: Maternal-fetal medicine visit 04/19/2022, about 18 weeks. Feels well; breathing at baseline, class II. BP normal. Anatomy scan normal. Echo with the PH team stable. Continue tadalafil, risperidone, prenatal vitamin. Cc: PCP.

documents.title: Prenatal visit note
documents.author: maternal-fetal medicine
documents.body: Maternal-fetal medicine prenatal visit 06/28/2022, 28 weeks. Doing well; PH symptoms stable, class II. BP normal. Fetal growth appropriate. Tdap given today. Continue current plan. Cc: PCP.

documents.title: Psychiatry update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry, visit 07/06/2022. Third trimester, no psychotic symptoms on risperidone 4 mg. We made a postpartum plan: protected sleep blocks with her husband covering nights, visit within two weeks of delivery, early call for any sleeplessness or suspicious thinking. Cc: PCP, MFM.

conditions.label: Supervision of high risk pregnancy, unspecified, unspecified trimester

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, labor and delivery. Admitted 08/17/2022, discharged 08/20/2022.

G1 at 35 weeks 1 day with pulmonary arterial hypertension on tadalafil, presented overnight for a blood pressure check; blood pressure 164/108 and 166/110 fifteen minutes apart. Urine protein/creatinine 1.4. Platelets and liver enzymes normal.

Diagnosis: preeclampsia with severe features.

Course: magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis through 24 hours postpartum; IV labetalol for severe-range pressures. Cardiac anesthesia and the PH team present; early epidural. Induction of labor, then vaginal delivery of a liveborn infant. No hemodynamic deterioration. Pressures under 140/90 by day 3 without oral agents.

Discharge medications: tadalafil 40 mg daily, risperidone 4 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin, icatibant as needed. No antihypertensive.
Follow-up: BP check with primary care within 10 days; PH center in 6 weeks; postpartum obstetric visit at 6 weeks. Return for headache, visual change or BP 160/110 or higher.

documents.title: Postpartum call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after the discharge summary arrived. Home since Saturday with the baby. Home cuff readings 120s to 130s over 80s. No headache, no vision change, breathing at her baseline, no leg swelling. Sleeping in shifts with her husband. Taking all meds including risperidone. Booked BP visit Monday 8/29.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Postpartum BP Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Twelve days after delivery at 35 weeks for preeclampsia with severe features. Brought the baby, who is feeding well.

No headache, no visual symptoms, no RUQ pain. Breathing at her usual. Tired in the ordinary newborn way. Sleep in pieces but she and her husband are trading nights, which her psychiatrist specifically wanted. No unusual thoughts; seeing psychiatry next week. PHQ-9 5.

BP 124/80 today. Lungs clear, loud P2 as before, no edema.

A/P
- Preeclampsia resolved; now history of severe preeclampsia, which raises her future cardiovascular risk and recurrence risk in any later pregnancy. Added to the problem list. Yearly BP and metabolic checks matter more now.
- PAH: PH center visit in October.
- Postpartum mood: low score, close psychiatry follow-up planned.
- Contraception: she will discuss with OB at 6 weeks.

documents.title: Postpartum visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body: Postpartum visit 09/28/2022, 6 weeks after delivery for severe preeclampsia. BP normal. Mood good. Exam normal. Contraception discussed in light of PAH; she declines a method. Future pregnancies: early care, preeclampsia risk reviewed. Cc: PCP.

documents.title: PH center follow-up
documents.author: pulmonary hypertension
documents.body: Regional pulmonary hypertension center. Visit 11/08/2022. Eleven weeks postpartum after preterm delivery for severe preeclampsia. PAH tolerated the pregnancy without decompensation. Functional class II. NT-proBNP 260. Exam: loud P2, no edema, JVP not raised. Continue tadalafil 40 mg daily. A further pregnancy would again carry high risk; she has not chosen a contraceptive method. Annual follow-up. Cc: PCP, MFM.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly visit, a bit late this year with the baby. Back at work since November.

Interval: delivery in August as documented, BP normal since. PH center in November: class II, stable on tadalafil. Psychiatry: stable through postpartum, no psychotic symptoms. Endocrinology to recheck prolactin when she is done nursing. No HAE attacks during or since the pregnancy.

Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily, tadalafil 40 mg daily, icatibant prn, prenatal vitamin.
PHQ-9 3.

Exam: BP normal. Heart regular, loud P2. Lungs clear. No edema. Weight down toward her baseline.

A/P
- History of severe preeclampsia: BP normal today; yearly lipids and A1c drawn.
- PAH, schizophrenia, prolactinoma: per specialists.
- Flu and bivalent COVID today.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cholesterol, A1c, kidney and liver tests all normal.

documents.title: Psychiatry update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry, visit 01/10/2023. Five months postpartum, she remains free of psychotic symptoms on risperidone 4 mg nightly. Mood good. Protected sleep plan with her husband worked well. Binge eating episodes rare. Continue current treatment; return in 3 months.

documents.title: Prior authorization: icatibant
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Yearly icatibant PA renewal. No attacks in the past year, plan still approves on-demand supply. Approved 2/15.

documents.title: RE: Pregnant again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Referral sent to the same group and marked urgent; I mentioned the PAH and the preeclampsia last time. Keep all your medicines going as before unless the PH team or psychiatry changes something. Let me know when your first visit is booked.

reports.text: Single intrauterine pregnancy with cardiac activity. Crown-rump length corresponds to 8 weeks. Ovaries unremarkable. No subchorionic collection.

documents.title: Initial prenatal visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
High-risk obstetrics group, regional hospital. Visit 06/20/2023.

33-year-old G2P0101 presenting for first prenatal care at 8 weeks by LMP. Prior delivery 10 months ago at 35 weeks for severe preeclampsia. Also PCOS, prolactin-secreting microadenoma, pulmonary arterial hypertension and hereditary angioedema; schizophrenia, stable.

Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily, tadalafil 40 mg daily, prenatal vitamin, icatibant 30 mg SC as needed. NKDA. No surgeries.
FH: father schizophrenia; mother and brother HAE; mother PCOS.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol, teacher.

BP 120/78, HR 72, BMI 26. Exam unremarkable.
Transvaginal ultrasound: viable intrauterine pregnancy at 8 weeks.

Plan: co-management with the PH center as in her first pregnancy; dating confirmed; routine first trimester labs; return in 6 weeks. Cc: PCP, PH center.

documents.title: Prenatal visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
High-risk obstetrics group. Visit 08/01/2023, 14 weeks 0 days.

Feels the pregnancy is going smoothly. Some tiredness and a little queasiness first thing in the morning, no vomiting. Eating normally; weight gain as expected for dates.
No palpitations, tremor, temperature intolerance, constipation, hair loss or skin changes.
FH: her mother developed hypothyroidism in her fifties.
SH: lives with her husband and their baby; teaching; no tobacco or alcohol.
Meds: risperidone 4 mg, tadalafil 40 mg, prenatal vitamin, icatibant as needed.

T 36.7 C (98.1 F), pulse 80, BP 114/72.
Exam: well. Thyroid normal in size, nontender. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Fundal height appropriate.

Plan: routine care, anatomy scan at 20 weeks, PH center review this month. Cc: PCP.

documents.title: PH center pregnancy review
documents.author: pulmonary hypertension
documents.body: Regional pulmonary hypertension center, visit 09/12/2023. 20 weeks pregnant. Functional class II, no decompensation. Continue tadalafil 40 mg daily. Delivery planning with obstetrics and cardiac anesthesia, target 37 weeks. Cc: PCP, OB.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 24 weeks pregnant, OB recommends both. Inactivated flu L deltoid, updated COVID R deltoid. No prior reactions. Observed 15 min, fine. Tdap planned at OB in a few weeks.

documents.title: Prenatal visit note
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body: High-risk obstetrics visit 11/07/2023, 28 weeks. Blood pressures normal throughout so far; no proteinuria. Fetal growth on track. PH center: stable class II on tadalafil. Tdap given. Delivery plan: scheduled induction at 37 weeks with cardiac anesthesia and the PH team available; HAE attack plan on file with the delivery unit. Cc: PCP.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, labor and delivery. Admitted 01/09/2024, discharged 01/11/2024.

G2P0101 at 37 weeks 0 days admitted for planned induction given pulmonary arterial hypertension and prior preterm delivery for severe preeclampsia. Blood pressures normal throughout the pregnancy and the admission; no features of preeclampsia this time.

Course: cervical ripening and oxytocin; early epidural with cardiac anesthesia following; PH team consulted daily. Vaginal delivery of a liveborn infant late on 01/09. Uneventful recovery, no hemodynamic concerns, no angioedema.

Discharge medications unchanged: tadalafil 40 mg daily, risperidone 4 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin, icatibant as needed.
Follow-up: PCP or OB BP check in 1 to 2 weeks; PH center in 3 months; postpartum visit at 6 weeks.

documents.title: Postpartum call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Two weeks after delivery. She and the baby are home and well; the older one is adjusting. Home BP readings normal all week. No headache or visual change, breathing as usual, no swelling. OB is doing her BP check at their postpartum visit, so no visit here needed now. Psychiatry appointment already set for next week.

documents.title: Postpartum visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body: Postpartum visit 02/20/2024, 6 weeks after induced vaginal delivery at 37 weeks. BP normal. Mood good. Exam normal. Contraception again discussed given PAH; she declines. Cc: PCP.

documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body: Outside endocrinology group. Visit 03/12/2024. Two pregnancies since her last visit with us, most recent delivery 01/09/2024; not breastfeeding now. No headaches, no visual symptoms, no galactorrhea. Prolactin 46 ng/mL. Will repeat pituitary MRI to confirm stability after two pregnancies. A dopamine agonist is not planned given PAH; observation if the lesion is stable. Cc: PCP.

documents.title: PH center follow-up
documents.author: pulmonary hypertension
documents.body: Regional pulmonary hypertension center. Visit 04/23/2024. Three months after a planned induction and uncomplicated vaginal delivery at 37 weeks. Functional class II. Six-minute walk 470 m. NT-proBNP 220. Loud P2, no edema. Continue tadalafil 40 mg daily. We reviewed again that pregnancy remains high risk; she is not using contraception. Next review in a year. Cc: PCP, OB.

documents.title: Swelling and refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: First attack in ages, left hand, after carrying the car seat around all day. Gave a dose at 5 and it's going down. Both my syringes are past their date anyway, can I get two new ones?

documents.title: RE: Swelling and refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent two to the specialty pharmacy. Glad it responded. Face or throat involvement still means the ED.

documents.title: Psychiatry update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry, visit 07/09/2024. Six months postpartum, stable. No psychotic symptoms; sleeping when the baby allows. Binge episodes rare. Risperidone 4 mg nightly continues.

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical specimen, satisfactory, endocervical/transformation zone cells present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First yearly visit here since 2022; the 2023 pregnancy kept her with OB.

Interval: second baby delivered 1/9 at 37 weeks by planned induction, no preeclampsia this time. PH center April: class II, walk distance up, tadalafil unchanged. Endocrinology: prolactin 46, MRI stable at 3 mm, watching without medication. Psychiatry: stable. One hand attack in June, home icatibant.

Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily, tadalafil 40 mg daily, icatibant 30 mg SC prn, prenatal vitamin.
PHQ-9 2.

Exam: BP normal. Thyroid normal. Breasts without masses. Heart regular, loud P2. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Pelvic normal, co-test collected. No edema.

A/P
- Cervical screening co-test.
- History of severe preeclampsia plus antipsychotic: lipids, A1c, CMP, CBC.
- PAH, prolactinoma, schizophrenia, BED: per specialists, all stable.
- Flu and COVID today.

documents.title: Pap and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Michelle, your Pap is normal with no HPV, next one in 2029. Cholesterol, A1c, blood count, kidney and liver numbers are normal.

documents.title: Psychiatry update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry, visit 01/14/2025. One year after her second delivery, no relapse of psychosis. Managing two young children and a full teaching load. Binge eating episodes infrequent; she uses CBT skills on her own. Risperidone 4 mg nightly continues. No EPS. Return in 3 months.

documents.title: Prior authorization: icatibant
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Insurer changed specialty pharmacies for the new plan year; icatibant needed a new PA. Submitted with HAE type I diagnosis and attack history. Approved 3/13. New pharmacy contacted pt to set up shipping.

reports.text: Comparison 2021. Left ventricle normal in size and systolic function. Right ventricular hypertrophy, unchanged. Valves normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Stable right ventricular hypertrophy; normal left ventricle.

documents.title: PH center annual review
documents.author: pulmonary hypertension
documents.body: Regional pulmonary hypertension center. Visit 05/13/2025. Functional class II, working full time, keeping up with two toddlers. NT-proBNP 190. Echo: RV hypertrophy unchanged, LV normal. Low-risk profile on tadalafil 40 mg daily; continue. Annual review. Cc: PCP.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body: Outside endocrinology group. Visit 06/17/2025. Asymptomatic. Cycles irregular in her PCOS pattern. Prolactin 41 ng/mL, stable. Continue observation; prolactin yearly, MRI only for symptoms or a rising level. Cc: PCP.

documents.author: front desk

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from September.

Interval: PH center May, low risk, echo stable. Endocrinology June, prolactin 41, observing. Psychiatry steady. No swelling attacks this year. Kids healthy now.

Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily, tadalafil 40 mg daily, icatibant prn, prenatal vitamin.
PHQ-9 3.

Exam: BP normal. Heart regular, loud P2. Lungs clear. No edema. Skin: mild jawline acne.

A/P
- Metabolic labs for risperidone and preeclampsia history.
- HAE: two in-date syringes confirmed.
- Pap next 2029.
- Flu and COVID today.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All of Tuesday's labs are normal. See you next fall unless something comes up sooner.

documents.title: Psychiatry update
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Outpatient psychiatry, visit 01/13/2026. Remains well on risperidone 4 mg nightly; no psychotic symptoms in many years. Binge eating disorder in good control. Continue; return in 3 months.

documents.title: Tadalafil shipment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The specialty pharmacy says they need a new prescription for tadalafil. Is that you or the PH center?

documents.title: RE: Tadalafil shipment
documents.author: RN

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Seen 07/03/2026.

CC: lip and tongue swelling.

HPI: 36-year-old woman with hereditary angioedema (C1 inhibitor deficiency) and pulmonary arterial hypertension on tadalafil arrives with two hours of steadily increasing swelling of the lips and tongue. No injury, no dental work, nothing new in her medicine list. She has had attacks before, in her hands and abdomen with severe abdominal pain, without clear trigger and settling over days, but never her mouth. No hives, itch or rash with any episode. She had not yet injected; her syringes were at home.
PMH: HAE; PAH; schizophrenia; PCOS; binge eating disorder; pituitary microadenoma; prior severe preeclampsia. No surgeries.
Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily, tadalafil 40 mg daily, prenatal vitamin, icatibant 30 mg SC as needed. NKDA.
FH: mother and brother with HAE.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol, teacher.

Exam: vital signs stable. Marked nonpitting edema of the lips and tongue, no erythema or warmth. No stridor, no drooling, voice normal, no respiratory distress. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No urticaria.

Labs: CBC and electrolytes normal. C1 inhibitor 6 mg/dL (low). C4 5 mg/dL (low). Tryptase 4.1 ng/mL (normal). Urine hCG negative.

MDM: bradykinin-mediated angioedema from known HAE, not histaminergic. Airway watched closely with ENT aware.
Treatment: icatibant 30 mg SC at 14:50. Swelling improving by 17:00, tongue near baseline at 20:30. Observed 6 hours, no airway compromise.

Disposition: discharged home. Follow up with primary care this week and with allergy/immunology to discuss preventive therapy. Return immediately for throat tightness, voice change or trouble swallowing. Advised to carry icatibant at all times.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called to let us know she went to the ED Friday for lip and tongue swelling, first time in her mouth. Got icatibant there, sent home that night. Today lips back to normal, no throat symptoms. Has two syringes at home and will keep one in her bag. ED records requested. Offered visit this week; she is away with family until August and asked for the first week back. Booked 8/6. Told her to use her icatibant and go to the nearest ED for any recurrence in the mouth or throat.

orders.reason: hereditary angioedema with first oropharyngeal attack; long-term prophylaxis

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after the 7/3 ED visit for lip and tongue swelling. ED record reviewed: C1 inhibitor and C4 low, tryptase normal, treated with icatibant and observed, no airway compromise.

No further attacks since. She had not had an episode involving her mouth before, and it frightened her. Carries a syringe in her school bag now and has one at home. Before that, one hand attack in 2024 and none in 2025.

Meds: risperidone 4 mg daily, tadalafil 40 mg daily, icatibant 30 mg SC prn, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: no lip, tongue or facial swelling. Oropharynx normal. Heart regular, loud P2. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
- Hereditary angioedema with a first oropharyngeal attack. Laryngeal risk is the concern now. She has not seen an immunologist in years; referral to allergy and immunology to discuss long-term prophylaxis and a written action plan. Continue icatibant on demand. ED for any throat symptoms even after injecting.
- Lipids and A1c today (annual risperidone monitoring, due anyway).
- PAH, prolactinoma, schizophrenia: stable with specialists.
Physical in November.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cholesterol and A1c from yesterday are normal. The allergy office has your referral.
